scope_note: REDUCED SCOPE, directed 2026-07: ARM A evaluated at all 6 budgets (the frontier curve, see arm_a_frontier below); ARM A vs ARM B paired comparison restricted to budget_fraction in {0.89, 0.94}, the only budgets where ARM B is latency-feasible -- see arm_b_latency_infeasible_note.

paired_comparison.no_gate_registered_note: Descriptive comparison only -- no pass/fail gate was registered for ARM A vs ARM B, unlike paired_eval.py's BOPs-vs-JOINT/JOINT-vs-STAGED comparisons.

arm_b_latency_infeasible_note: ARM B (uniform-r ToMe, r in 1..11) is LATENCY-INFEASIBLE at 77/79/82/85% of identity latency under the measured LUT: uniform merging pays this device's fixed per-merge overhead at 11 sites, whereas TANDEM's concentrated <=2-point schedules reach 76.5% of identity. This is a measured hardware finding about merge PLACEMENT granularity, independent of accuracy.
arm_b_d_pred_limitation_note: ARM B's D_pred is not reported (null in frontier_plans.csv) -- P2.1's own Dm_table.csv only covers TANDEM's registered plan-space grid (MERGE_BLOCKS=(1,3,5,7,9,11) x MERGE_RS=(32,64,98,128), 24 rows total, confirmed by direct read), not ARM B's uniform-every-block r in {1..11}. Extrapolating a new accuracy-damage model here would be fabricating data this project has not measured; the real comparison is the MEASURED top-1 accuracy reported below, not a predicted proxy.
pre_registered_interpretation: This compares merge-PLACEMENT granularity (TANDEM's <=2-point schedules) against uniform-r merging at matched MEASURED latency -- the hardware analogue of the P2.2 saturation finding. It is NOT a joint-vs-staged test (void per CHARACTERIZATION.md).
